campaign.title: The Wells Remember
campaign.premise: A caravan crosses a recovering ashland as a spreading water shortage turns ordinary trade into a contest over trust, access, and the future of the region.
campaign.player_role: A newly independent caravan master with enough capital to survive one bad season, but not enough to ignore the people who control the roads.
campaign.regional_objective: Keep the five-settlement water network alive long enough to decide who will control its future.

chapters.title: The First Ledger
chapters.summary: Learn the region’s price differences, hire a first companion, and complete one profitable or politically useful delivery.
chapters.player_question: Can I make money without treating every settlement as a mark?

chapters.title: Thin Wells
chapters.summary: The water shortage becomes visible. Prices move, rumors conflict, and both factions ask the caravan to prove its loyalty.
chapters.player_question: Who deserves scarce water, and what does helping them cost elsewhere?

chapters.title: The Empty Reservoir
chapters.summary: The region reaches a dangerous shortage. The caravan must choose between exploiting the price, building trust, or spending its capital on shared infrastructure.
chapters.player_question: Is survival enough if the network that made survival possible collapses?

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Resolve the shortage through an alliance, regulated control, private profiteering, or an expensive act of shared repair.
chapters.player_question: What kind of region did my choices make possible?

factions.name: The Ash Wardens
factions.public_position: Stability requires rules, escorts, and controlled access to vital roads and wells.
factions.private_pressure: Their officials fear losing authority more than they fear being wrong.
factions.content_rule: A Warden choice should trade volatility for control, never read as simply good.

factions.name: The Free Caravans
factions.public_position: Goods move when people are allowed to move, bargain, and take risks without a permit.
factions.private_pressure: Their leaders can mistake freedom for the right to leave weaker settlements behind.
factions.content_rule: A Caravan choice should trade access for instability, never read as simply good.

factions.name: The Cinder Riders
factions.public_position: Keep the Old Road open for frontier families and independent movement.
factions.private_pressure: Armed escorts can become coercive when route power grows faster than legitimacy.
factions.content_rule: A Rider choice should trade movement and escort safety against intimidation and conflict.

factions.name: The Salt Crown
factions.public_position: Restore shared cistern law and defend the basin’s water sources.
factions.private_pressure: Stable water access can become a monopoly enforced by armed power.
factions.content_rule: A Crown choice should trade water stability against permits, tolls, and monopoly pressure.

locations.name: Ashgate
locations.story_function: The place where the player learns that every transaction has a witness.
locations.visual_motif: Black gate timbers, white chalk ration marks, and Warden lanterns in straight rows.
problems: officials hiding how low the reserve really is

locations.name: Brine Cross
locations.story_function: The first settlement to reveal that water can be both a commodity and a public promise.
locations.visual_motif: Salt-white basins, blue rope bridges, and empty jars hung as warning bells.

locations.name: Cinderford
locations.story_function: A place where scrap and charcoal can become infrastructure, if someone can keep the furnaces fed.
locations.visual_motif: Red furnace mouths, chain lifts, and soot-dark workers under yellow awnings.

locations.name: Hollow Market
locations.story_function: The most profitable and least trustworthy market, where every rumor has a price.
locations.visual_motif: Canopy tunnels, colored cloth flags, and goods displayed in old shell craters.

locations.name: Reedwatch
locations.story_function: The settlement that makes distant consequences impossible to ignore.
locations.visual_motif: Reed roofs, watchfires reflected in shallow water, and hand-painted missing-person boards.

characters.name: Nara Vey
characters.motivation: Prove that the roads can be read by people rather than owned by officials.
characters.strength: Turns uncertain route information into a clearer forecast and spots alternate approaches.
characters.fear: Being trapped in a place where every exit has been bought by someone else.
characters.relationship_hook: Nara respects a player who shares useful route information, but distrusts secret toll deals.

characters.name: Jorun Pale
characters.motivation: Keep the caravan alive through disciplined provisions and honest weights.
characters.strength: Reduces provision waste and identifies cargo choices that will create a fragile run.
characters.fear: Watching people gamble with supplies because the ledger makes the risk look abstract.
characters.relationship_hook: Jorun approves of recovery plans and loses trust when the player knowingly abandons dependents.

characters.name: Tess Oryn
characters.motivation: Turn personal connections into a network no faction can close completely.
characters.strength: Creates additional negotiation choices and softens the reputation cost of compromise.
characters.fear: Being remembered only as the person who made bad bargains sound reasonable.
characters.relationship_hook: Tess likes decisive compromises but challenges the player when charm replaces a material solution.

events.title: The Gatekeeper's Chalk
events.setup: A fresh chalk mark on the wagon says the toll doubled overnight. The gatekeeper insists the old price was a clerical error.

choices.label: Pay the new toll and keep moving.
choices.visible_result: The road is safe today, but the Wardens learn that your caravan can be pressured.

choices.label: Ask Nara or Tess to challenge the ledger.
choices.visible_result: You lose time but expose a pattern of invented tolls.

choices.label: Turn back and take the exposed road.
choices.visible_result: The caravan keeps its margin and accepts a danger it can see.

events.title: The Span at Cinderford
events.setup: A bridge has dropped one side into the ash. A foundry crew can make it passable, but only if someone supplies the missing scrap and charcoal.

choices.label: Give the crew the materials from your hold.
choices.visible_result: The road opens for everyone, not just your caravan.

choices.label: Pay a ferry crew and protect the cargo.
choices.visible_result: You preserve the delivery but leave the bridge problem behind.

choices.label: Sell or leave the heaviest cargo and cross light.
choices.visible_result: The caravan moves, but a buyer at the destination may receive less than promised.

events.title: The Last Clean Barrel
events.setup: A settlement committee offers nearly any price for one clean barrel. Behind them, families wait with smaller containers and no bargaining power.

choices.label: Sell to the committee at the peak price.
choices.visible_result: The ledger looks excellent. The settlement report does not.

choices.label: Break the barrel into a fair ration sale.
choices.visible_result: You earn less, but the market stays open and the settlement remembers the fairness.

choices.label: Keep it for the caravan’s next route.
choices.visible_result: You preserve your recovery margin and accept that someone else pays the shortage.

events.title: Three Riders, No Banner
events.setup: Three riders offer to escort the caravan through the ash. They know the road too well and refuse to say who paid them.

choices.label: Hire them and keep the cargo moving.
choices.visible_result: The road is safer, but the riders now know what your caravan carries.

choices.label: Demand names and a destination before agreeing.
choices.visible_result: You lose time and learn which faction is trying to move water without a ledger.

choices.label: Refuse, then warn the next settlement.
choices.visible_result: The caravan remains exposed, but the network gains a warning.

tracks.name: Caravan Capability
tracks.purpose: Improves the caravan without removing the need to choose a route.

nodes.choice_created: carry a second contract or a recovery reserve
buy water earlier without wasting the margin
accept uncertainty with a stated source

tracks.name: Network Trust
tracks.purpose: Unlocks relationship-driven solutions and changes which settlements will ask for help.

nodes.choice_created: see who benefits from a price movement
choose between factions instead of taking the only offer
spend capital to alter the crisis rather than merely trade around it

milestones.condition: crisis_stage >= 1 and log contains shortage report
complete a route after a failed or sacrificed event

endings.title: The Wells Remember Everyone
endings.summary: The caravan spends its advantage on a shared water network. Trade becomes slower and more accountable, but no single faction can close every well.
endings.crew_note: Jorun stays to audit the new stores; Nara maps the public routes.

endings.title: The Wells Belong to Those Who Carry
endings.summary: Official relief never arrives, but ordinary charcoal trade and direct support turn Reedwatch's improvised water exchange into a durable public institution.
endings.crew_note: Nara marks the Commons fires as permanent landmarks; Jorun records the deliveries that kept them lit.

endings.title: Order at the Cistern
endings.summary: The Wardens secure the reservoirs and the roads become safer, but permits and ration rules decide who may trade.
endings.crew_note: Tess calls it a victory with a locked door.

endings.title: No Road Owns the Sky
endings.summary: Independent caravans keep the region supplied through a web of informal routes. Prices stay volatile, but access remains open to those willing to take the risk.
endings.crew_note: Nara leaves a route book in every settlement, with the dangerous pages marked honestly.

endings.title: The Best Margin
endings.summary: The caravan becomes the region’s indispensable broker. The crisis ends for the markets that can pay first, while the player inherits a profitable network built on uneven recovery.
endings.crew_note: Jorun asks whether a full ledger can still be called honest when half the region is missing from it.
